agree.reason: Signed training records, two clean state audits and a training cut from 20 to 12 hours give a skeptical HR manager concrete reasons to phone-screen a teacher, but the letter says nothing about when she could start or when she is free to interview, so the manager can't act on it right away.

honest.reason: The letter rightly drops the unprovable 'cut your training in half' claim, but 'without leaving out any procedures' and 'every student passes a quiz before working at the bench' are small additions that the facts don't directly support.

works_the_facts.reason: The numbers appear only in raw form: the letter never says the training was cut 40% (8 hours saved per new teacher), that the pass rate rose 17 points (about 40% relative), or that the labs have gone seven years without a serious injury.

right_comparison.reason: The before-and-after comparisons (20 to 12 hours, 41% to 58%) are accurate, but neither one is turned into a size or rate the reader could compare against her own plant.

qualification.reason: The GMP gap comes with a checkable completion date of May 2, but the hard June 14 start constraint is left out, and the LMS gap has no timeframe for learning it.

objections.reason: The 'teachers don't know regulated work' objection is met head-on with audit-proof signed records and the GMP course, but the reader's practical questions about start date and interview availability go unanswered even though the facts supply the answers.

fit.reason: It is a proper one-page cover letter addressed to the named manager, though it has no contact details, and the November date sits oddly beside the spring-break and May course timeline.
